name: xml-coreutils
desc: Powerful interactive system for text processing
why: An old interactive system that treats text processing as XML pipelines is a genuinely odd old-school environment.

brief.what_it_is: xml-coreutils is a collection of Unix/POSIX command-line tools for processing XML files, modeled on GNU coreutils. The homepage describes it as 'command line tools for XML processing' and says its aim is to make XML processing for shell users 'exactly as easy as text processing.' The executables listed include xml-cat, xml-cp, xml-cut, xml-grep, xml-sed, xml-awk, xml-wc, xml-ls, xml-less and others, each named after its text-tool counterpart with an xml- prefix. The homepage does not spell out the input and output formats for each tool beyond saying they work on XML files.
brief.why_it_exists: The homepage says the goal is to make XML processing for shell users as easy as text processing, and that the tools aim to stay as close as possible to GNU coreutils. An essay on the project site explains this in more detail; I did not read it.
brief.how_it_works: The homepage does not explain the internal mechanism. It names two dependencies for building from source: the Expat XML parser library, and the S-Lang terminal services library.

commands_seen.context: Unpacks the downloaded 0.8a source tarball, per the homepage's install walkthrough.
Configures the build with a chosen install prefix; the path is a placeholder.
Runs the project's test suite. The homepage says it 'will produce a lot of output, but hopefully won't produce any errors.'
Installs the built tools to the configured prefix.

brief.install_notes: Building from source needs a C compiler and related build tools, plus the Expat XML Parser Library and the S-Lang terminal services library. The homepage says both are standard packages in major Linux distributions. Source is a tarball such as xml-coreutils-0.8a.tar.gz, installed with the standard configure/make/make check/make install sequence. The contrib page covers DEB and RPM packages, which I did not open. Nothing in the homepage mentions Homebrew, macOS, or Windows.
brief.standout: The project's stated design goal is to mirror GNU coreutils almost one-to-one, with an xml- prefix on each familiar tool, so shell users can apply the same habits to XML. The scout note calls it an 'interactive system'; the homepage instead describes a set of command-line tools, and the only interactive-looking one in the list is xml-less, so the 'interactive environment' framing should not be repeated without checking.
brief.status: Unknown from the homepage alone. The homepage says the project 'is still at an early stage, and is not ready for production use.' It names 0.8a as the example tarball but gives no release date, no last-commit date, and no changelog. The homepage has a SourceForge portal link and a mailing list link, but I did not check either for activity.
brief.caveats: The homepage explicitly says the project is early-stage and not ready for production use, though it is usable for simple tasks. It needs Expat and S-Lang available at build time. The homepage does not list supported platforms beyond Unix/POSIX and Linux distributions. The brew formula's caveats field is empty, and the brew description ('Powerful interactive system for text processing') does not match what the homepage describes. The homepage says the code is GPL v3 or later.
